Context compression is the art of keeping what matters while discarding what doesn't. When you're working with large language models, context window limits become a real constraint. You can't just throw everything at the model and hope for the best.

The key insight is that not all text is equally important. Some paragraphs contain the core information you need. Others are padding, boilerplate, or redundant restatements of things already said. A good compression algorithm identifies these patterns and keeps the signal while removing the noise.

Modern tokenizers like tiktoken can tell you exactly how many tokens a piece of text will consume. Armed with this information, you can make intelligent decisions about what to keep and what to cut.
